title: Basic Economic Problems
summary: Explore the fundamental economic problem of resource scarcity, the four factors of production, the three central questions (What, How, and For Whom to Produce), and opportunity cost versus sunk costs.

title: Break-Even Analysis and Cost-Volume-Profit
summary: Master Break-Even Analysis (CVP Analysis), algebraic formulas for BEP, Margin of Safety, target profit planning, graphical charts, and step-by-step solved numericals.

title: Budget Line and Price Line
summary: Understand the consumer's budget constraint, the algebraic derivation of the budget line, vertical and horizontal intercepts, the price-ratio slope (-Px/Py), and graphical shifts versus rotations.

title: Class 11 Economics: Growth and Development
summary: Distinguish rising output from broader development and evaluate poverty, inequality, employment, and human resources together.

title: Class 11 Economics: Basic Concepts and Resources
summary: A clear starting point for scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, and the resources used in production.

title: Class 11 Economics: Mathematics for Economic Problems
summary: A practical method for solving equations, percentage changes, tables, and common economics numericals.

title: Class 11 Economics: Elasticity and Consumer Behaviour
summary: Understand responsiveness, utility, consumer choice, and the meaning of consumer surplus.

title: Class 11 Economics: Money and Inflation
summary: Understand the functions of money, money supply, inflation, deflation, and their effects on households and firms.

title: Class 11 Economics: National Income
summary: Organise GDP and related income measures, compare the main approaches, and avoid double counting.

title: Class 11 Economics: Nepal’s Economy and Resources
summary: Use economic concepts to study Nepal’s natural resources, agriculture, industry, tourism, transport, and communication.

title: उपभोक्ता व्यवहारका गणितीय समस्याहरू र समाधान (Consumer Behaviour Numerical Problems & Solutions)
summary: सीमान्त उपयोगिता ह्रास नियम र सम-सीमान्त उपयोगिता नियमसम्बन्धी ६ वटा परीक्षा लक्षित संख्यात्मक समस्याहरूको चरणबद्ध समाधान तथा स्व-मूल्याङ्कन अभ्यास।

title: उपभोक्ता र उपभोक्ताको व्यवहार (Meaning of Consumer and Consumer Behaviour)
summary: उपभोक्ताको अर्थ, उपभोक्ताको व्यवहारको परिभाषा, उपभोक्ताका प्रकारहरू, अध्ययनको आवश्यकता, निर्णय प्रक्रिया र आर्थिक विवेकशीलताको विस्तृत अध्ययन।

title: उपभोक्ताको बचत/अधिशेष र उत्पादकको बचत/अधिशेष (Consumer Surplus & Producer Surplus)
summary: उपभोक्ताको बचत (अधिशेष) र उत्पादकको बचत (अधिशेष) को अवधारणा, बजार सन्तुलनमा CS र PS को अन्तरक्रिया तथा कुल सामाजिक कल्याण (आर्थिक अधिशेष) को अधिकतमकरण, विस्तृत रेखाचित्र र संख्यात्मक समस्या समाधान।

title: मागको छड्के लोच र यसका प्रकारहरू (Cross Elasticity of Demand & Types)
summary: मागको छड्के लोचको अर्थ र सूत्र, प्रतिस्थापक, पूरक र असम्बन्धित वस्तुहरूको विश्लेषण, तथा २ वटा उदाहरणीय संख्यात्मक समस्याहरूको विस्तृत समाधान।

title: मागको सिद्धान्त (Theory of Demand)
summary: प्रभावकारी मागको अवधारणा, रैखिक माग समीकरण (Qd = a - bP) को विस्तृत व्याख्या, मागको नियम, माग वक्ररेखा तलतिर झुक्नुका कारणहरू, अपवादहरू, तथा माग रेखामा हुने चाल र स्थानान्तरण।

title: मागको मूल्य लोचका निर्धारक तत्वहरू र महत्त्व (Determinants & Importance of Price Elasticity)
summary: कुनै वस्तुको माग किन लोचदार वा बेलोचदार हुन्छ भन्ने प्रमुख निर्धारक तत्वहरू, तथा व्यावसायिक निर्णय, मूल्य निर्धारण रणनीति र सरकारी आर्थिक नीतिमा मागको लोचको व्यावहारिक महत्त्व।

title: लोचको अर्थ र प्रकारहरू (Meaning of Elasticity)
summary: लोचको सामान्य अवधारणा, रबर ब्यान्डको भौतिक दृष्टान्त, लोचको आधारभूत सूत्र, मागको लोचका प्रकारहरू (मूल्य, आय, र छड्के लोच), तथा आपूर्तिको लोचको संक्षिप्त परिचय।

title: माग र आपूर्तिको लोचका गणितीय समस्याहरू र समाधान (Elasticity Numerical Problems and Solutions)
summary: प्रतिशत विधि, कुल खर्च विधि, बिन्दु विधि, आय लोच, छड्के लोच, तथा आपूर्ति लोचका परीक्षा लक्षित गणितीय समस्याहरूको चरणबद्ध समाधान र स्व-मूल्याङ्कन अभ्यास।

title: बजार सन्तुलनका गणितीय समस्याहरू र समाधान (Market Equilibrium Numerical Problems and Solutions)
summary: रैखिक माग र आपूर्ति समीकरणबाट सन्तुलन मूल्य र परिमाण गणना, तालिका निर्माण, रेखाचित्र विश्लेषण, तथा परीक्षा लक्षित अभ्यास प्रश्न र समाधान।

title: मागको आय लोच र यसका प्रकारहरू (Income Elasticity of Demand & Types)
summary: मागको आय लोचको अर्थ, सूत्र, प्रकारहरू (धनात्मक, ऋणात्मक, र शून्य), वस्तुहरूको वर्गीकरण (सामान्य, विलासी र निम्नस्तरीय), तथा उदाहरणीय संख्यात्मक समाधान।

title: सीमान्त उपयोगिता ह्रास नियम (Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility)
summary: गोसेनको पहिलो नियम, सीमान्त उपयोगिता ह्रास नियमको अर्थ, मान्यताहरू, तालिका र रेखाचित्र, अपवादहरू, तथा विस्तृत आलोचना र महत्त्व।

title: प्रतिस्थापनको नियम वा सम-सीमान्त उपयोगिताको नियम (Law of Substitution / Equi-Marginal Utility)
summary: गोसेनको दोस्रो नियम, सम-सीमान्त उपयोगिता नियमको अर्थ, उपभोक्ता सन्तुलनका सर्तहरू, तालिका र रेखाचित्रद्वारा विस्तृत व्याख्या, आलोचना र महत्त्व।

title: बजार सन्तुलन र मूल्य निर्धारण (Market Equilibrium and Price Determination)
summary: माग र आपूर्तिको अन्तरक्रिया, सन्तुलन मूल्य र सन्तुलन परिमाणको निर्धारण, अतिरिक्त माग (अभाव) र अतिरिक्त आपूर्ति (बचत) को आत्म-समायोजन संयन्त्र, तथा माग र आपूर्तिमा हुने स्थानान्तरणको प्रभाव।

title: अर्थशास्त्रको अर्थ र परिभाषाहरू (Meaning and Definitions of Economics)
summary: अर्थशास्त्रको शाब्दिक उत्पत्ति, विकासक्रम तथा एडम स्मिथ (सम्पत्ति), अल्फ्रेड मार्शल (कल्याण), र लियोनेल रोबिन्स (दुर्लभता र छनोट) का प्रमुख परिभाषाहरूको तुलनात्मक र आलोचनात्मक विश्लेषण।

title: मागको मूल्य लोच र यसका प्रकारहरू (Price Elasticity of Demand and Its Degrees)
summary: मागको लोचको अर्थ, मागको मूल्य लोचको अवधारणा र सूत्र, तथा मूल्य लोचका पाँच प्रकारहरू वा डिग्रीहरूको विस्तृत व्याख्या, तालिका र रेखाचित्र।

title: उत्पादनको सिद्धान्त (Theory of Production)
summary: उत्पादनको अर्थ, उत्पादन फलन (अल्पकालीन र दीर्घकालीन), कुल, औसत र सीमान्त उत्पादन बीचको सम्बन्ध, परिवर्तनशील अनुपातको नियम (तीन चरणहरू), तथा पैमानाको प्रतिफलको नियमको विस्तृत अध्ययन।

title: आपूर्तिको मूल्य लोच (Price Elasticity of Supply)
summary: आपूर्तिको मूल्य लोचको अर्थ र सूत्र, आपूर्तिको लोचका पाँच प्रकारहरू वा डिग्रीहरू, ज्यामितीय व्याख्या, तथा आपूर्तिको लोच निर्धारण गर्ने प्रमुख तत्वहरूको विस्तृत अध्ययन।

title: आपूर्तिको सिद्धान्त (Theory of Supply)
summary: आपूर्तिको अवधारणा, मौज्दात र आपूर्ति बीचको भिन्नता, रैखिक आपूर्ति समीकरण (Qs = c + dP) को व्याख्या, आपूर्तिको नियम, तालिका, वक्ररेखा, निर्धारक तत्वहरू, तथा आपूर्तिमा हुने चाल र स्थानान्तरण।

title: उपयोगिताको अवधारणा र दृष्टिकोणहरू (Concept of Utility and Approaches)
summary: उपयोगिताको परिभाषा, गणनावाचक र क्रमवाचक दृष्टिकोणको तुलना, कुल उपयोगिता र सीमान्त उपयोगिता बीचको सम्बन्ध, तथा TU र MU गणना अभ्यास।

title: Class 11 Economics: Production and Cost
summary: Learn how firms transform inputs into output and how total, average, marginal, and cost measures fit together.

title: Banking and Monetary Policy
summary: Understand the banking system, money creation, and the tools used to influence monetary conditions.

title: Cost Concepts and Cost Curves
summary: Build cost tables and explain the relationships among total, average, and marginal cost.

title: Development Economics: Poverty, Inequality, and Employment
summary: Distinguish growth from development and evaluate poverty, inequality, unemployment, and human resources together.

title: Economic Systems and the Production Possibility Curve
summary: Compare ways of organising an economy and use the production possibility curve to explain choice and efficiency.

title: Factor Pricing: Rent, Wages, Interest, and Profit
summary: Study how the factors of production are rewarded and use the existing rent note as the starting point for distribution theory.

title: Government Finance and Fiscal Policy
summary: Organise public revenue and expenditure and explain how fiscal policy can influence the economy.

title: Price and Output under Imperfect Competition
summary: Compare monopoly and other imperfectly competitive markets through demand, revenue, and equilibrium output.

title: International Trade and Trade Policy
summary: Use comparative advantage to explain trade and evaluate tariffs, quotas, and other trade-policy choices.

title: Market and Revenue Curves
summary: Read market demand and connect total, average, and marginal revenue for different sellers.

title: Development Planning in Nepal
summary: Understand why development plans are prepared and how goals, resources, implementation, and evaluation fit together.

title: Nepal’s Foreign Trade and Foreign Employment
summary: Connect trade, migration, remittances, and employment challenges to Nepal’s economic choices.

title: Price and Output under Perfect Competition
summary: Explain firm equilibrium in perfect competition using revenue, cost, and profit conditions.

title: Quantitative Techniques for Economics
summary: Build a repeatable method for averages, dispersion, index numbers, and clear economic interpretation.

title: Critically explain the Risk Bearing Theory of Profit.
summary: The Risk Bearing Theory of Profit was propounded by Professor Hawley in 1907.

title: Sustainable Development Goals and Nepal
summary: Use the SDG framework to connect economic, social, and environmental dimensions of development in Nepal.

title: Subsistence Theory of Wage
summary: Explain why classical economists believed wages tend to return to the subsistence level and evaluate the theory’s limitations.

title: Wage Fund Theory of Wages
summary: Wage Fund Theory states that average wages are determined by dividing a predetermined wage fund by the number of workers employed: (W = Total Wage Fund / No. of Workers) . It explains why average wages fall when more workers share a fixed fund. However, the theory is unrealistic because the wage fund is not always fixed, workers are not homogeneous, wages are not perfectly flexible, and labour demand depends on product demand, productivity, and institutions. Thus, it is mainly important as a classical theory of wages.

title: Classical Theory of Interest
summary: The Classical Theory of Interest provides a foundational framework for understanding how interest rates are determined through the interaction of supply and demand for capital.

title: Consumer Equilibrium Numericals
summary: Master mathematical problem-solving for consumer equilibrium under Indifference Curve analysis, budget line equations, MRS calculations, and utility-maximization baskets.

title: Consumer's Surplus and Producer's Surplus
summary: Learn the concepts of Consumer Surplus, Producer Surplus, and Total Economic Welfare, including graphical representations, measurement formulas, and practical business applications.

title: Cost-Plus and Mark-Up Pricing
summary: Learn the principles of Cost-Plus / Mark-Up Pricing, mathematical price formulas, linkage between optimal mark-ups and price elasticity, and practical hospitality applications.

title: Cross Elasticity of Demand
summary: Explore how the demand for one commodity responds to price changes in related goods, analyzing substitute goods, complementary goods, and unrelated goods with diagrams.

title: Demand, Supply, and Market Equilibrium Numericals
summary: Master mathematical solutions for linear demand and supply equations, market equilibrium determination, shortage/surplus calculations, and elasticity problems.

title: Determination of Consumer's Equilibrium
summary: Master how consumer equilibrium is determined under Indifference Curve analysis, the first-order tangency condition (MRSxy = Px/Py), second-order convexity, and disequilibrium adjustments.

title: Differences Between Microeconomics and Macroeconomics
summary: Compare microeconomics (individual consumer, firm, and market choices; Price Theory) and macroeconomics (economy-wide aggregates, GDP, inflation, unemployment, and monetary/fiscal policy; Income Theory).

title: Duopoly Cournot and Bertrand Models
summary: Explore duopoly market structures, comparing Augustin Cournot's quantity competition model and reaction curves with Joseph Bertrand's price competition model and the Bertrand Paradox.

title: Economies and Diseconomies of Scale
summary: Explore internal and external economies and diseconomies of scale, their role in determining the shape of the Long-Run Average Cost curve, and strategic product pricing applications.

title: Exceptional Shapes of Indifference Curves
summary: Explore non-standard indifference curves, including straight linear curves for perfect substitutes, L-shaped curves for perfect complements, upward-sloping curves for economic bads, and circular curves.

title: FACTOR PRICING: RENT CONCEPT
summary: Rent is payment for using production factors; contract rent is tenant-landlord gross payment, while economic rent is surplus from fixed supply. Ricardo argued rent stems from fertility differences: superior land earns differential rent over marginal no-rent land, through extensive or intensive cultivation. Critics note fertility changes, accessibility, uses, and scarcity.

title: Factors Determining Elasticity of Demand
summary: Explore the primary economic and behavioral determinants that make consumer demand price-elastic or price-inelastic, with practical industry examples.

title: Fundamental Concepts, Efficiency, and Time Element
summary: Master core decision-making principles (opportunity cost, incremental reasoning, discounting), technical and economic efficiency, accounting vs. economic profit, and Marshallian time horizons.

title: Importance of Elasticity in Decision Making
summary: Master how price, income, and cross elasticity guide business pricing strategies, Total Revenue maximization, monopoly price discrimination, taxation policies, and international trade.

title: Income Consumption Curve (ICC) and Price Consumption Curve (PCC)
summary: Explore the Income Consumption Curve (ICC) for normal and inferior goods, the Price Consumption Curve (PCC), and the ordinal derivation of the downward-sloping demand curve.

title: Income Elasticity of Demand
summary: Understand how changes in consumer income affect the demand for goods, classifying commodities into normal, luxury, necessity, and inferior goods.

title: Income Effect, Price Effect, and Substitution Effect
summary: Master the decomposition of the total price effect into substitution and income effects, exploring Hicksian and Slutsky methods across normal, inferior, and Giffen goods.

title: Indifference Curve and Indifference Map
summary: Understand the geometric concept of an Indifference Curve (Iso-Utility Curve), the construction of an indifference schedule, and how an Indifference Map represents a consumer's complete scale of preferences.

title: Introduction to Demand, Concepts, and Determinants
summary: Define effective economic demand, explore individual vs. market demand, derived vs. direct demand, the mathematical demand function, and key demand determinants.

title: Introduction to Ordinal Utility Analysis
summary: Discover the foundations of modern Ordinal Utility Theory developed by Hicks and Allen, including historical evolution, core behavioral axioms, and superiority over cardinal utility.

title: Introduction to Supply and the Law of Supply
summary: Understand the economic concept of supply, passive vs. active factors of production, the Law of Supply, movements along versus shifts in the supply curve, and key supply determinants.

title: The Law of Demand and Its Exceptions
summary: State and explain the Law of Demand, its underlying assumptions, demand schedule, downward-sloping curve, why it slopes downwards, and key exceptions.

title: Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility
summary: Master Gossen's First Law of Consumption (Law of DMU), underlying assumptions, TU and MU schedules and curves, the Point of Satiety, consumer equilibrium, and real-world business applications.

title: Law of Substitution or Equi-Marginal Utility
summary: Learn Gossen's Second Law (Law of Equi-Marginal Utility), its mathematical equilibrium condition, tabular schedule demonstration, and multi-commodity resource allocation.

title: The Law of Returns to Scale (Long-Run Production)
summary: Explore long-run production dynamics using Isoquants, Isocost lines, Producer Equilibrium (Least-Cost Combination), the Expansion Path, and the three phases of Returns to Scale (IRS, CRS, and DRS).

title: The Law of Variable Proportions (Short-Run Production)
summary: Master the Law of Variable Proportions (Law of Diminishing Returns), its three operational stages, mathematical relationships between TP, AP, and MP, and why Stage II is the rational stage of production.

title: Aggregate Demand and Its Derivation
summary: Explain how the aggregate-demand curve connects the price level with equilibrium output.

title: Aggregate Supply and Output Adjustment
summary: Introduce short-run and long-run aggregate supply and explain how firms respond to prices and costs.

title: Equilibrium and Methods of Macroeconomic Analysis
summary: Distinguish equilibrium from disequilibrium and introduce static, comparative-static, and dynamic analysis.

title: Balance of Payments and External Accounts
summary: Organise current, capital, and financial transactions with the rest of the world.

title: Banking and Central Banking
summary: Explain commercial-bank functions, deposit creation, central-bank roles, and the financial system’s macroeconomic importance.

title: Government Budget and Deficit Financing
summary: Read the main parts of a government budget and explain revenue deficits, borrowing, and deficit financing methods.

title: Business Cycles and Economic Fluctuations
summary: Identify business-cycle phases and the demand, supply, financial, and expectation forces behind fluctuations.

title: Circular Flow of Income and Expenditure
summary: Trace income, output, and expenditure through two-sector, three-sector, and open-economy models.

title: Classical Theory of Employment and Output
summary: Introduce the classical view of employment, wages, prices, output, and the role of flexible markets.

title: Fiscal and Monetary Policy in the Closed Economy
summary: Compare how fiscal and monetary changes affect output and interest rates through the IS-LM framework.

title: Consumption Function and Determinants
summary: Introduce the consumption function, its technical properties, and the variables that influence household spending.

title: Theories of Consumption Behaviour
summary: Compare absolute-income, relative-income, life-cycle, and permanent-income explanations of consumption.

title: Macroeconomics and the Digital Economy
summary: Connect digital production, platforms, data, and changing business models with macroeconomic outcomes.

title: Classical and Keynesian Employment: Evaluation
summary: Compare classical and Keynesian explanations of employment, output, and policy effectiveness.

title: Exchange Rates and Exchange-Rate Regimes
summary: Explain exchange rates, purchasing-power and market forces, and the difference between fixed and flexible regimes.

title: Financial and Capital Markets with Financial Inclusion
summary: Distinguish money and capital markets and explain how access to finance affects macroeconomic participation.

title: Fintech, Digital Money, and Decentralised Finance
summary: Introduce financial innovation and consider its effects on money, payments, credit, and policy oversight.

title: Fiscal Federalism and Public–Private Partnerships
summary: Introduce the allocation of public finance across levels of government and the logic of public–private partnerships.

title: Fiscal Policy and Fiscal Multipliers
summary: Explain fiscal-policy objectives, instruments, automatic stabilisers, and the limits of multiplier estimates.

title: Globalisation, Foreign Direct Investment, and the Global Economy
summary: Assess trade, capital flows, global integration, and foreign direct investment as macroeconomic forces.

title: Economic Growth, Development, Poverty, and Inequality
summary: Distinguish growth from development and connect productivity, poverty, inequality, employment, and sustainable progress.

title: Income Determination in Two, Three, and Four-Sector Models
summary: Build equilibrium income models by adding households, government, and the external sector to aggregate expenditure.

title: Inflation: Concepts, Causes, Measurement, and Effects
summary: Define inflation, distinguish major causes, and assess how changing prices affect households and firms.

title: Interest Rates, Bond Prices, and the Liquidity Trap
summary: Connect bond prices with interest rates and explain the Keynesian liquidity-trap idea.

title: Macroeconomics: Scope and Method
summary: Understand economy-wide analysis and the main questions asked about output, employment, prices, and growth.

title: Investment Function and Investment Demand
summary: Explain the types, determinants, and uncertainty involved in business investment decisions.

title: Investment Theories: MEC, Accelerator, and Tobin’s q
summary: Introduce marginal efficiency of capital, accelerator, neoclassical, and Tobin’s q approaches to investment.

title: The IS-LM Model
summary: Derive the product-market and money-market equilibrium schedules and locate short-run output and interest-rate equilibrium.

title: Keynesian and Classical Aggregate Supply
summary: Compare Keynesian, intermediate, and classical views of output adjustment and policy effects.

title: Keynesian Effective Demand
summary: Use aggregate expenditure and effective demand to explain output and employment when resources are underused.

title: Macroeconomic Variables, Stocks, and Flows
summary: Classify important macroeconomic variables and distinguish stock measures from flow measures.

title: Money, Interest, and Exchange-Rate Links
summary: Connect monetary conditions, interest rates, capital flows, and exchange-rate pressure in an open financial system.

title: Monetary Policy: Objectives and Instruments
summary: Describe the goals, types, instruments, and transmission channels of monetary policy.

title: Money Supply and Demand for Money
summary: Introduce the functions of money, determinants of money supply, and Keynesian motives for holding money.

title: Multiplier Analysis and Its Extensions
summary: Explain the investment, government-expenditure, tax, balanced-budget, and foreign-trade multipliers.

title: The Mundell–Fleming Open-Economy Model
summary: Use a simple open-economy framework to compare fiscal and monetary policy under fixed and flexible exchange rates.

title: National Income Aggregates and Their Interpretation
summary: Relate GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, national income, personal income, disposable income, and per-capita income.

title: Methods and Difficulties of National Income Measurement
summary: Compare the product, income, and expenditure methods and identify practical measurement difficulties.

title: Phillips Curve and Expectations
